metadata.description: Rule set for detecting student-targeted internship, job, and gig scams in India

reportingChannels.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
reportingChannels.description: Ministry of Home Affairs portal for financial fraud and cyber crime reporting. Dial 1930 immediately if money has been sent.

reportingChannels.name: Chakshu (Sanchar Saathi - DoT)
reportingChannels.description: Department of Telecommunications platform to report suspected fraud communications via SMS, WhatsApp, or calls.

reportingChannels.name: AICTE Official Internship Portal
reportingChannels.description: Official portal for AICTE internship verification. AICTE mandates that all internships are strictly zero-fee for students.

rules.title: Demand for upfront registration or processing fee
rules.explanation: Real companies never charge you an application, registration, or processing fee to give you a job or internship.

source.name: CERT-In Advisory CIAD-2024-0050 & RBI BE(A)WARE Booklet

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Low. Legitimate exam bodies (like UPSC/GATE) charge exam fees, but private company job offers or internships should never demand upfront payments.

rules.title: Payment demanded for laptop, uniform, or training kit
rules.explanation: Legitimate employers never make candidates pay for laptops, IDs, training kits, or dispatch courier charges.

source.name: RBI BE(A)WARE Booklet (Section on Job Frauds)

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Low. Employers either supply equipment free of charge or require you to use personal devices; they never sell equipment via UPI/chat transfers.

rules.title: Direct personal UPI ID, QR code, or crypto payment request
rules.explanation: Companies process finances through official corporate banking channels, not personal UPI IDs or QR codes on WhatsApp/Telegram.

source.name: I4C / Ministry of Home Affairs Task Scam Advisory

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Medium. May trigger if discussing peer-to-peer payments or splitting college bills, but in an offer letter/recruitment context, it is a critical red flag.

rules.title: Task-based gig, YouTube like, or review rating scam
rules.explanation: Paying money to perform simple tasks like 'liking YouTube videos' or 'rating hotels' is the hallmark of I4C-warned part-time task fraud.

source.name: I4C (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre) Task Fraud Advisory

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Very low. Major digital platforms prohibit paid engagement schemes; legitimate corporate internships do not offer per-like commissions.

rules.title: Unrealistic daily income for minimal or non-technical effort
rules.explanation: Promises of earning Rs 2,000–10,000 daily for typing, copy-pasting, or 1–2 hours of work are standard bait used by scammers.

source.name: FTC Job Scams Guidance & I4C Public Advisories

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Medium. Genuine high-paying consultant roles exist, but unsolicited student messages offering guaranteed daily payouts for basic typing are almost always scams.

rules.title: Immediate job offer or selection without interview or application
rules.explanation: Reputable companies do not issue instant selection letters or high-paying internships without a structured interview or assessment.

source.name: RBI BE(A)WARE Booklet & CERT-In Advisory CIAD-2024-0050

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Low. Walk-in drive notifications may invite candidates without prior interviews, but they do not claim you are already selected with an offer letter.

rules.title: Request for OTP, banking credentials, or PIN before joining
rules.explanation: Never share an OTP, ATM PIN, UPI PIN, or bank password. No recruiter ever needs your OTP or bank security codes.

source.name: RBI Kehta Hai / Cyber Crime Security Guidelines

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Very low. Authentic onboarding portals have secure document upload steps after an offer is formalized; they never demand OTPs or payment PINs over chat.

rules.title: Artificial urgency, extreme time pressure, or fear tactics
rules.explanation: Scammers create artificial pressure (e.g. 'offer expires in 15 minutes') to stop you from researching or asking advice.

source.name: UK NCSC Phishing Guidance & CISA Email Scam Advisory

rules.falsePositiveRisk: High as an isolated signal (marketing promotions and campus drive deadlines often have deadlines). Used as an auxiliary weight.

rules.title: Corporate recruiter using free public webmail (@gmail, @yahoo)
rules.explanation: Recruiters from established organizations (e.g. TCS, Infosys, Amazon) always use their corporate domain email, never generic @gmail.com or @yahoo.com.

source.name: Google Anti-Phishing Guidelines & AICTE Caution Notice

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Low for claims representing large IT/MNC brands. Early-stage student startups may occasionally use Gmail, but established recruiters never do.

rules.title: Redirecting official corporate business to Telegram or WhatsApp
rules.explanation: Scammers shift conversations to Telegram or WhatsApp to evade enterprise email security filters and delete chat histories.

source.name: I4C Advisories on Telegram/WhatsApp Job Recruitment Fraud

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Medium. Some modern recruiters use WhatsApp for interview reminders, but conducting the entire interview/hiring on Telegram is characteristic of fraud syndicates.

rules.title: Obfuscated URL shortener hiding the real destination
rules.explanation: Shorteners like bit.ly, tinyurl, and cutt.ly hide the true website address, preventing you from seeing the actual target domain before clicking.

source.name: UK NCSC Phishing Guidance & OWASP URL Handling Guidelines

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Medium. Legitimate SMS notifications occasionally use short links due to character limits, but students should never click unverified short links.

rules.title: Direct IP address host instead of registered domain name
rules.explanation: Authentic company career portals have domain names (e.g. company.com). Direct raw IP addresses (e.g. http://192.0.2.1) indicate temporary scam infrastructure.

source.name: OWASP Unvalidated Redirects and URL Security Guidelines

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Very low. No commercial job board or enterprise employer sends students to naked IP addresses.

rules.title: Punycode or IDN homograph character substitution
rules.explanation: Attackers substitute Cyrillic or special lookalike characters in brand names (showing as 'xn--...' in the URL) to disguise fake domains.

source.name: OWASP Guidance on Internationalized Domain Name (IDN) Homograph Attacks

rules.title: URL contains '@' symbol trick to mislead the reader
rules.explanation: In standard URLs, everything before an '@' sign is treated as username/password, and the browser actually connects to the host *after* the '@'.

source.name: OWASP URL Parsing & Unvalidated Redirects Guidelines

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Very low. Legitimate career links never contain '@' credentials in the URL authority section.

rules.title: Known company brand placed in subdomain or path of untrusted domain
rules.explanation: A link like 'tcs.careers-portal-india.com' is hosted on 'careers-portal-india.com', NOT TCS. Scammers put brand names in subdomains to trick you.

source.name: Google Phishing Guidance & OWASP Link Parsing

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Low to medium. Requires checking whether the base domain is the official verified corporate domain.

rules.title: Use of high-abuse top level domains (TLD) for official branding
rules.explanation: Enterprise recruiters in India operate on .com, .in, or .org. Domains ending in .xyz, .top, .buzz, or .click are frequently exploited for ephemeral scam sites.

source.name: CERT-In Phishing Advisories & Spamhaus Threat Analytics

rules.falsePositiveRisk: Medium. Some startups use .site or .online, but multinational IT recruiters do not host recruitment drives on high-abuse cheap TLDs.

rules.title: Typo-squatted or lookalike domain of a verified enterprise
rules.explanation: This domain is suspiciously close to an official recruiting portal (e.g. 'infosys-jobs.com' or 'tcs-portal.net') but is not registered by the actual company.
rules.falsePositiveRisk: Low when matched against established corporate brand names.

fictionalTestCases.input: Dear Student, congratulations! You are selected for TCS Part-Time Online Internship. Daily income ₹2500 for YouTube video like and subscribe tasks. To activate your student employee portal, kindly pay a refundable registration fee of Rs 499 to hr-tcs-verify@okhdfcbank. Connect immediately on Telegram: t.me/tcs_careers_hr

fictionalTestCases.description: Laptop courier charge + OTP demand on WhatsApp
fictionalTestCases.input: Dear candidate, you are appointed as Data Entry Executive at Infosys without any interview. A company laptop and training kit will be dispatched to your home address. Pay dispatch courier charges of ₹1,200 via UPI QR code. Send screenshot and share OTP received on your mobile. Offer expires in 30 minutes.

fictionalTestCases.description: Lookalike link with brand in subdomain + risky TLD
fictionalTestCases.input: Infosys Campus Recruitment 2026! Complete your profile here: http://infosys.campus-hiring-drive.xyz/apply and earn 5000 daily.

fictionalTestCases.description: Startup hiring via WhatsApp reminder with slight urgency
fictionalTestCases.input: Hi! We saw your profile for a front-end internship role at our studio. A few slots remain open for screening this week. Connect with our coordinator on WhatsApp: wa.me/919876543210 if you are interested in scheduling an introductory call.

fictionalTestCases.description: Legitimate TCS campus drive invitation via official portal
fictionalTestCases.input: Dear Candidate, Thank you for registering for the TCS National Qualifier Test (TQT). Your test slot is scheduled on Saturday. Please log in to your dashboard at https://nextstep.tcs.com/campus/ to download your hall ticket. TCS does not charge any application or placement fee at any stage.

Greetings from the AICTE Internship Portal. You have applied for the Web Development Internship. Shortlisted candidates will be invited for a technical interview round by the recruiting organization. Track your application status directly at https://internship.aicte-india.org. Never share OTP or payment details.
